title: Buddy Rotation Sprint and Skills Decomposition — 90d Onboarding Accelerator
body:
Purpose:
This doc outlines an experimental 90-day ‘Buddy Rotation Sprint’ designed to accelerate ramp for new engineers while validating role fit early. The approach intentionally exposes new hires to multiple adjacent teams (serving runtime, infra, console, SRE) for short rotations so that we: 
- reduce single-buddy bottlenecks
- surface strengths/interest areas early
- create a shared cross-team context for first major deliverables

Scope and intended audience:
- Audience: People Ops, hiring managers, onboarding buddies, hiring committee, hiring managers of eng subteams
- Roles: IC Software Engineer (new grad to senior IC), Staff/Lead hires use a modified version (longer rotations)
- Timeline: 0–90 days post start date

High-level goals (measurable):
- Time-to-first-PR-with-approver: target <= 21 days
- Time-to-produce-impacting-deliverable: target <= 60 days (small feature/bugfix)
- Manager confidence (survey) at 90d >= 4/5
- Role-fit clarity vote (hire/role-shift/extend probation) at 90d

Format: Buddy Rotation Sprint (sample cadence)
- Week 0 (preboarding): paperwork, environment, reading list, intro 1:1 with hiring manager and program owner
- Week 1: Primary buddy shadow + orientation + mini goals (read codebase, setup, first ticket)
- Weeks 2–4: 2-week micro-rotation cycle across two teams (each rotation = 5 working days):
  - Rotation A (serving-runtime): focus - inference path tracing, local dev, tiny bug fix
  - Rotation B (console/ops): focus - reproduce UI bug, run local dashboards, follow a trace
- Weeks 5–8: Longer contributor block (4 weeks) on a primary team with weekly rotation check-ins and incremental deliverables
- Weeks 9–12: Ownership sprint — candidate owns a small scoped project and does a public wrap-up

Buddy rotation logistics (ops notes):
- Primary buddy remains constant for culture/feedback thread; rotation buddies assigned per cycle
- Each rotation has a 30-min kickoff + 30-min wrap w/ buddy and rotation owner
- Rotation checklist (to be completed & signed): environment validated, at least 1 minor change merged, knowledge note added to team playbook
- Calendar templates: onboarding calendar with blocked focus windows + shadow sessions (see linked artifacts)

Skill decomposition & role-fit rubric (use during week 4 and week 12 reviews) — flat 1–5 scoring with defined anchors:
- Core engineering: code quality, debugging, testing, understanding of LLM/inference tradeoffs (1=needs heavy coaching, 5=autonomous)
- Systems thinking: ability to map request->serving->storage, identify failure modes
- Product sense: translate customer requirement into acceptance criteria
- Collaboration & communication: cross-team syncs, async docs, PR hygiene
- Operations readiness: running local infra, perf profiling, reproducing incidents
- Learning velocity: ramping on new stacks, consuming documentation, asking right questions

Week-4 quick calibration (sample guidance):
- If Core engineering <=2: extend focused pairing 2 more weeks, assign small focused tasks with explicit acceptance criteria
- If Systems thinking <=3: schedule 1:1 with infra lead + focused troubleshooting exercise
- If Learning velocity <=2: add weekly structured reading + weekly quiz/checklist

Interview calibration & internal rubric notes (for hiring managers & interviewers)
- Use same competency buckets for interviews to improve continuity between hiring signal and onboarding evaluation
- Scoring guidance: 1–2 = major gaps / fail, 3 = meets baseline, 4 = strong, 5 = exceptional. Panel average <=2.5 -> do not extend offer without remediation plan
- Panel composition suggestions: 1 hiring manager, 1 peer IC from primary team, 1 cross-team engineer (serving/runtime or infra), 1 PM or product-adjacent when appropriate
- Practical tasks during onsite/remote interview: small debugging exercise with given traces, architecture sketch (30 mins), coding task focused on correctness + tests

Sample interview questions mapped to competencies (short list):
- Core engineering: "Walk me through a bug you recently fixed end-to-end; how did you reason about the fix?"
- Systems thinking: "Given a spike in inference latency for short inputs, what layers would you investigate first and why?"
- Product sense: "How would you prioritize improving latency vs. model quality for a revenue-generating feature?"
- Collaboration: "Describe a time you changed your approach because of feedback from a reviewer."

New-hire checklist (preboarding -> 30d -> 60d -> 90d)
- Preboarding: accounts provisioned, laptop imaged, docs sent (read list), intro Slack, first-week schedule
- Day 1–7: local dev + one small merged PR, meet 1:1s with cross-team leads, add to rotation schedule
- Day 8–30: complete two rotations, join team standups, deliver first minor feature or bugfix, 2x feedback check-ins
- Day 31–60: contribute to primary team's backlog, own end-to-end ticket, lead a tech demo to team
- Day 61–90: finish ownership sprint, present outcomes to broader org, 90d manager & peer reviews collected

90d evaluation template (to be completed by manager + primary buddy):
- Role-fit recommendation: keep / role-shift / extend-probation
- Competency scores (six buckets above) with short evidence bullets (3–5 lines each)
- Candidate strengths & recommended development areas
- Candidate self-assessment attached

Operational KPIs to track (people-ops + hiring metrics):
- Median time to first merged PR (by cohort)
- % of hires reaching manager confidence >=4 at 90d
- % of hires needing extended probation
- Net new hires that changed role alignment within 180 days (measure whether rotations reduced churn/mis-hire)

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to scale rotations for bigger cohorts without overloading rotation buddies? (Option: rotate buddies over 2-week mini-cohorts)
- Should rotations be mandatory for senior IC hires or optional? Recommend opt-in with mandatory core shadowing week
- Create light-weight scoring form for week-4 calibration (Google sheet template) — assigned to Anika
- Automate calendar creation via HR onboarding flow — owner: Marcus (work with infra)

Appendix: sample week-1 micro-schedule (editable)
- Mon: 09:00 intro w/ manager, 10:30 env setup, 14:00 buddy walkthrough
- Tue: first small ticket assigned, pairing sessions 11:00 & 15:00
- Wed: rotation kickoff prep docs, team lunch, reading list check
- Thu: shadow on incident postmortem, small PR created
- Fri: wrap w/ buddy + week1 retro + list of 3 goals for next rotation

Notes to reviewers (people-ops/hiring managers):
- This is intentionally experimental — pilot with 6 hires in Q3 and collect quantitative + qualitative signals.
- Please comment on the week-4 calibration thresholds (are they too conservative?).
- We will iterate rubric anchors after first cohort to better align with staffing levels across Dedicated/Private product teams.

End of doc.
